reading_scope.boundary_declaration: Strictly limited to the specified sections; explicitly disclaiming complete reading of all 176 pages.

evidence_entries.content: Potential energy W_pot(beta, gamma) = H_p + 1/2 C beta^2 + sqrt(5/(4pi)) * [k beta cos(gamma) / (4j(j+1))] * [3 Omega^2 - j(j+1)]. For j > 3/2, the lowest state occurs for Omega = j, gamma = pi (oblate), with equilibrium deformation beta = sqrt(5/(4pi)) * (k/C) * (2j-1)/(4(j+1)).
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Theoretical model expression within single-j particle-surface coupling

evidence_entries.content: Surface kinetic energy partitioned into vibrational T_vib and rotational T_rot. T_rot = (hbar^2 / (2 J_3)) (K - Omega)^2 + (hbar^2 / (4 J_1) + hbar^2 / (4 J_2)) [I(I+1) - K^2 + j(j+1) - Omega^2 - (-)^(I-j)(j+1/2)(I+1/2) delta_{Omega, 1/2} delta_{K, 1/2} a], with hydrodynamic irrotational moments J_kappa = 4 B beta^2 sin^2(gamma - kappa * 2pi/3).
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Theoretical kinetic energy formulation showing Coriolis decoupling term for Omega=1/2

evidence_entries.content: Breakdown of axial strong-coupling product solution for j=3/2: W_pot has equal values for (Omega=3/2, gamma=pi) and (Omega=1/2, gamma=0), lacking a distinct gamma-minimum and requiring coupled differential equations.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Author-recognized failure condition of axial symmetry / strong coupling

evidence_entries.content: Intermediate coupling region analyzed via weak-coupling phonon expansion (N <= 4 for j=3/2, Fig. 4) and semi-classical solution for j >> 1 (Eq. II.27: <j_z>/j = 1 - 1/(j+1) * x^2/sqrt(x^4 + 4/9)). Hydrodynamic coupling parameter x = 0.9 j^(-1/2) (A=20) to 1.4 j^(-1/2) (A=200) indicates single-particle systems fall in intermediate coupling unless multiple particles cooperate.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Theoretical calculation demonstrating angular momentum transfer to surface

evidence_entries.content: Many-particle strong surface coupling: particles move independently in the deformed potential characterized by Omega_p, filling pairwise with opposite Omega_p; total Omega = sum Omega_p. Ground state has I = K = Omega (Omega=0 for even configurations). Effective coupling scales as n * x, ensuring strong coupling far from closed shells.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Theoretical model for multi-particle deformation alignment

evidence_entries.content: Competition between surface coupling and particle residual forces: weak forces preserve independent Omega_p motion (Fig. 6a); strong short-range forces couple particles to a resultant J first, which then couples to surface (Fig. 6b). Surface coupling dominates in heavier nuclei and large deformations, while particle forces are prominent in light nuclei and near closed shells.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Qualitative physical model boundary acknowledged by authors

evidence_entries.content: Rotational spectrum of even-even nuclei: E_I = (hbar^2 / (2 J)) I(I+1) for I = 0, 2, 4..., even parity, with J = 3 B beta^2. Centrifugal and gamma-vibrational distortions introduce corrections delta E_I propto - I^2(I+1)^2. Empirical E(2+) drops by a factor of ~50 from closed shells to mid-shell (Fig. 13).
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Theoretical rotor spectrum compared with broad empirical systematics

evidence_entries.content: Measured energies and E4:E2 ratios in even-even nuclei with A > 140: Hf178 (E2=89, E4=289 keV, ratio=3.2), Hf180 (93, 307 keV, 3.3), Ra226 (67, 217 keV, 3.2), Th230 (58, 187 keV, 3.2), Th232 (50, 167 keV, 3.3), Pu238 (43, 146 keV, 3.4), confirming convergence to the theoretical ratio 10:3 = 3.33 for large deformations, while Pb208 has E2=2614, E4=3200 keV, ratio=1.2 and Sm150 has ratio=2.3.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Empirical nuclear spectroscopy data compiled from 1952-1953 literature

evidence_entries.content: Authors contrast their model with particle-recoupling models (Horie et al. 1951, Flowers 1952b): while valence recoupling can explain 2+ spins, it fails to explain the dramatic 50-fold energy drop across shells, the 3.33 ratio, uncrossed E2 cascades (15:11:7:3), and massive E2 enhancements.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Historical methodological critique of alternative explanations

evidence_entries.content: Deformation comparison for rotational states: Dy160 (E2=85 keV, F=80, beta_E=0.65, beta_Q=0.28), Er166 (80 keV, F=140, beta_E=0.65, beta_Q=0.31), Yb170 (84 keV, F=180, beta_E=0.62, beta_Q=0.27), Hf176 (89 keV, F=120, beta_E=0.58, beta_Q=0.24), Os186 (137 keV, F=55, beta_E=0.45, beta_Q=0.15). beta_E exceeds beta_Q by a factor of ~2.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Direct experimental accounting identifying a factor-of-two systematic discrepancy

evidence_entries.content: Authors attribute the discrepancy (beta_E > 2 beta_Q) to either the inadequacy of the hydrodynamic collective deformation formula for Q_0 or an underestimate of the mass parameter B / moment of inertia J_irrot, realizing that the simple irrotational liquid drop model is quantitatively incomplete.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Authors open self-critique of the hydrodynamic inertia model

evidence_entries.content: Modern connection: 1953 model coordinates (beta, gamma, theta_i) and D_2 symmetry are inherited by 5DCH and algebraic collective models; however, modern pairing-induced moment of inertia (0.3-0.5 J_rigid), Nilsson deformed orbitals, microscopic 3D angular momentum projection (VAP/PAV), magnetic scissors modes (1+), and triaxial wobbling/chirality must NOT be anachronistically imputed to the 1953 text.
evidence_entries.epistemic_status: Agent epistemological boundary analysis distinguishing historical origin from modern development
